<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD defines a standard source download from the project's official GitHub repository using a tagged release tarball over HTTPS. The `source` array entry is a direct, predictable URL pointing to versioned upstream content. There are no command substitutions, dynamic downloads, or remote code execution mechanisms in the global scope or in `pkgver()`, which is absent (so the top-level `pkgver` variable is used directly).

The commands `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` and `makepkg --printsrcinfo` will only fetch and extract the specified tarball and parse the PKGBUILD metadata. No build or prepare functions are executed due to the flags used, and there is no active code in `pkgver()` or at the top level that would perform malicious actions during sourcing. The b2sums checksum is present and valid, though even if it were 'SKIP', that alone would not make this step unsafe.

This package follows standard AUR packaging practices with no signs of injected malicious logic in the scope relevant to these commands.
</details>
<evidence>

</summary>
